title: Excel for Data Analytics & Data Engineering
description: Job-ready formulas, functions, cleaning, lookups, statistics, dates, PivotTables and Power Query.

blocks.text:
1. How to use this guide
This is a practical Excel syllabus for a fresher targeting Data Analyst, BI Analyst, Reporting Analyst, or Data Engineer roles.
You do not need every Excel function ever created. The functions in this guide cover the functions that are most useful for
cleaning, transforming, joining, validating, summarizing, analyzing and reporting data.
Recommended practice order: Basics -> Conditional logic -> Aggregation -> Lookups -> Text cleaning -> Dates ->
Statistics -> Dynamic arrays -> Error handling -> PivotTables -> Power Query -> Projects.
Example dataset used throughout: an Excel table named Sales with columns such as OrderID, Date, Customer, Region, Product,
Category, Quantity, UnitPrice, Discount, Revenue, Cost, Profit and Status.
Important: Excel formulas use commas in many installations. Some regional settings use semicolons instead. If a formula gives a
separator error, replace commas with semicolons.

23. Interview cheat sheet
Question
Strong answer
XLOOKUP vs VLOOKUP?
XLOOKUP is more flexible: it can look left/right, has exact match as the natural choice, and can return a custom
not-found result.
SUMIF vs SUMIFS?
SUMIF handles one condition; SUMIFS handles multiple conditions.
COUNT vs COUNTA?
COUNT counts numeric cells; COUNTA counts non-empty cells.
IFERROR vs IFNA?
IFERROR catches all Excel errors; IFNA specifically catches #N/A.
INDEX + MATCH?
A flexible lookup pattern that separates finding a position from returning a value.
Why use Power Query?
To build repeatable data import and transformation steps instead of manually cleaning data every day.
Why use PivotTables?
To quickly summarize large datasets by dimensions and measures.
Why use Excel Tables?
They provide structured references, automatic expansion and cleaner formulas.

26. One complete project to build
E-commerce Sales & Data Quality Dashboard
Use a dataset containing OrderID, OrderDate, CustomerID, Product, Category, Region, Quantity, UnitPrice, Discount, Revenue,
Cost and Status.
Step 1: Import CSV -> Step 2: Convert to Table -> Step 3: Clean with Power Query -> Step 4: Validate duplicates/nulls -> Step
5: Create calculated columns -> Step 6: Build PivotTables -> Step 7: Create charts -> Step 8: Publish the summary in Power BI
-> Step 9: Document the logic on GitHub.
Profit = Revenue - Cost

Profit Margin = IFERROR(Profit / Revenue, 0)
Net Revenue = Revenue * (1 - Discount)
Recommended KPIs: Total Revenue, Total Profit, Profit Margin, Orders, Customers, Average Order Value, Top Product, Top
Region, Monthly Growth.

result, and automate the repeatable steps. That is the Excel skill that transfers directly into SQL, Python, Power BI and Data Engineering.
